name: Olum, PRL 81, 3567 (1998): superluminal travel requires negative energies -- no staticity, no sphericity, no foliation

source.located: arXiv:gr-qc/9805003v2 (14 Oct 1998), Ken D. Olum, Tufts; Phys. Rev. Lett. 81, 3567 (1998). 8 pages, eqs (1)-(11), Figs 1-5, refs [1]-[8].
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9805003, all 8 pages returned; every quotation below is from that text.

published_statement: Abstract: 'I propose a definition of superluminal travel which requires that the path to be traveled reach a destination surface at an earlier time than any neighboring path. With this definition (and assuming the generic condition) I prove that superluminal travel requires weak-energy-condition violation.'  Condition 1 (p.4): 'a causal path P is superluminal from A to B only if ... There exist 2-surfaces Sigma_A around A and Sigma_B around B such that (i) if p in Sigma_A then a spacelike geodesic lying in Sigma_A connects A to p, and similarly for Sigma_B, and (ii) if p in Sigma_A and q in Sigma_B then q is in the causal future of p only if p = A and q = B.'  Theorem (p.6): 'any spacetime that admits superluminal travel on some path P (and thus, according to our definition, that satisfies Condition 1) and that satisfies the generic condition on P, must also violate the weak energy condition at some point of P.'  Proof: P is a null geodesic normal to both surfaces; theta-hat = 0 at A (Sigma_A extrinsically flat); Raychaudhuri eq. (3) with omega = 0, WEC => R_ab K^a K^b >= 0, generic => shear not identically 0, so theta-hat < 0 at B (eq. 4); but Condition 1 forces theta-hat >= 0 at B (eqs 5-8): contradiction.  Two further things the paper states that the tree does not: (a) p.4, the condition 'might not be sufficient for what one would call superluminal travel, because it is possible that while P arrives earlier than any nearby path, it is still slower than a path some larger distance away'; (b) p.3, a SEPARATE special-case argument for a spacetime flat outside a bounded region: a causal path with t2 - t1 < x2 - x1 forces WEC violation 'somewhere' in the modified region via Tipler's and Hawking's CTC theorems (no singularities, generic condition in the region) -- that is the only reference-geometry ('lead') statement in the paper, and its conclusion is not localised to the path.
published_hypotheses: H1 Condition 1: 2-surfaces Sigma_A, Sigma_B each swept by a one-parameter family of spacelike geodesics through A (resp. B), with no causal relation between the surfaces except A -> B (p.4). Used: theta-hat = 0 at A needs Sigma_A extrinsically flat at A; the z < 0 sign at B needs (ii).

H2 The generic condition holds on P: some point of P with K_[a R_b]cd[e K_f] K^c K^d != 0 (p.4; Hawking-Ellis). Used: shear cannot vanish identically, so theta-hat < 0 strictly at B. Olum: 'holds whenever there is any normal matter or any transverse tidal force anywhere on P'.
H3 The weak energy condition on P, used only through R_ab K^a K^b >= 0 on the null tangent K (i.e. the NEC on P; Einstein's equation assumed, G = c = 1).

H4 Smooth spacetime in which P actually reaches B (p.6: singularities are no alternative 'other than by making the purported path not actually reach the destination'); no staticity, no symmetry, no global foliation, no global hyperbolicity, no asymptotic flatness assumed.

H5 (special case, p.3 only) spacetime flat outside a bounded region t > t0, x in [x1,x2], ...; no singularities; generic condition in the modified region; conclusion WEC violated somewhere in the region -- via Tipler 1976/1977 and Hawking 1992, NAMED-NOT-READ here.
hypothesis_drift: ACCURATE, no drift: driven.py:109-114 restates H1 (as 'arriving earlier than every neighbouring path'), H2, H3 and H4, and 'at some point OF THAT PATH ... not averaged' matches p.6 'at some point of P'. driven.py:46-50, :484 (DOCKET_PREMISE_WAS_TRUE = False, 'Olum 1998 needs no staticity') and foliation.py:75 ('no staticity, no sphericity and no foliation') are correct: the proof uses only Riemannian normal coordinates near B and a local t = 0 hypersurface, no foliation.

DROPPED H2 (generic condition): ledger.py:393-397 (D5), spec.py:106-107 and :198, composite.py:116-117, foliation.py:74-77 and :235-240 ('with the NEC' only), specthm.py:1354-1371 -- none names the generic condition; without it the conclusion fails (rederivation (3): shear identically zero gives theta(B) = 0, no contradiction). driven.py:111 alone keeps it.

DROPPED H1's construction: ledger.py:394-395 states the conclusion 'pointwise on the path travelled' with the hypothesis reduced to 'no staticity, no symmetry, no sphericity'; the 2-surface geodesic construction that makes theta-hat = 0 at A and forces z < 0 at B is nowhere in the ledger row (owner None, CITED).

REPLACED H1 by a different notion -- 'a lead relative to a reference geometry': spec.py:106-107 'by Olum there cannot be [a lead] without negative energy', spec.py:198, specthm.py:1367-1371 'a lead needs negative energy (D5 ... no symmetry assumed)', specthm.py:2835-2837 (V1 'the lead'), foliation.py:235-240 (D4 'arrives EARLIER than in the reference geometry ... REPLACED BY A STRONGER ONE: Olum, Gao-Wald, VBL'). Olum's general theorem compares P with NEIGHBOURING paths (Condition 1), and he says on p.4 it may not be sufficient for superluminal travel in the reference-geometry sense. His only reference-geometry result is the p.3 special case (H5): flat outside a bounded region, WEC violated SOMEWHERE in the region, not on the path. The tree's 'lead needs negative energy' therefore rests on H5, a narrower class with a weaker (non-pointwise) conclusion, or on VBL/Gao-Wald -- and VBL is perturbative and, per Gao-Wald p.3, gauge-dependent (a pure-gauge h_ab opens the light cones everywhere), while Gao-Wald Theorem 1 gives 'little control over the size of the region K'' (their p.10). 'REPLACED BY A STRONGER ONE' at foliation.py:240 overstates the three papers jointly.

CONCLUSION RELOCATED off the path: composite.py:116-117 cites Olum 'for the requirement of negative energy, which this configuration supplies', while composite.py:90-93 has the early ray crossing only vacuum (T_kk = 0 along the whole path, exotic matter 'somewhere the payload never goes'). Olum's conclusion is WEC violation AT A POINT OF P. Rederivation (4): a vacuum ray with non-zero Weyl shear has theta(B) < 0, so it cannot satisfy Condition 1 -- unless a conjugate point precedes B, which composite.py itself asserts, and then the ray is not achronal and H1 fails on that ground. Either way the configuration does not instantiate Olum's theorem; the citation attributes to it a statement it does not make. Not a refutation of composite's own early-arrival computation, which is Gao-Wald Jacobi-matrix optics and is not this audit's object.

STRENGTH UNDERSTATED (not in M's favour either way): the proof uses only R_ab K^a K^b >= 0, i.e. the NEC on P; 'WEC' in the title and in driven.py:112, ledger D5 is the weaker-sounding form. foliation.py:240 ('with the NEC') is the sharper reading. Under a modified gravity where Einstein's equation is replaced, the theorem becomes 'superluminal travel requires null-convergence-condition violation on P' (as Santiago-Schuster-Visser 2105.03079 sec. 6 say of their own result) -- no owner states this scope limit.

Olum's own caveat on the CTC extension (p.6: the theorem cannot be extended into a CTC-containing region because the 2-surfaces cannot be built there) and on the Casimir example (p.7: 'not clear whether this phenomenon is sufficient ... does not account for the mass of the plates') are not carried by any owner; neither bears on how the tree uses the result.

data_at_publication.quantity: Casimir stress tensor between conducting plates, T_ab = (pi^2/720 d^4) diag(-1,1,1,-3) (eq. 9), giving R_ab K^a K^b = -2 pi^3/(45 d^4) (eq. 10)
data_at_publication.value_then: pi^2/720 d^4 (1998, textbook electromagnetic Casimir result)
data_at_publication.value_now: unchanged: the same coefficient in every later restatement read (Lobo-Crawford 2002 eq. 32); rederived here: sympy gives -2 pi^3/(45 d^4) exactly. Lobo-Crawford eq. (33) prints -2 pi^2/(45 d^4), a factor-pi misprint in the RESTATEMENT, not in Olum.
data_at_publication.source_now: standard QED Casimir result, not re-measured in this pass (no PDG entry; not an input to the theorem)
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: no -- the number is an illustration of the loophole (quantum fields violate WEC), not an input; the theorem itself takes no numerical datum

rederivation.outcome: 0 failures over 23 checks (sympy 1.14.0 + z3 5.1.0 + RK4 numerics). (1) eq. (1) is flat: Riemann = 0 symbolically, x' = x(1-t^2) pulls back to Minkowski, null rays match eq. (2), x = t/(1-t^2) is the right-going ray; arrival at x = 1 is t = (sqrt5-1)/2 = 0.618034 -- the paper prints '(1+sqrt5)/2 ~ 0.618', which is 1.618: a MISPRINT, recorded as a discrepancy, not an error in the theorem. (2) Casimir: R_ab K^a K^b = -2 pi^3/(45 d^4) exactly as eq. (10); Lobo-Crawford's restatement is off by a factor pi. (3) Raychaudhuri step: theta' = -R_kk - 2 sigma^2 - theta^2/2 with theta(0) = 0, R_kk >= 0, sigma not identically 0 gives theta(B) < 0 on four profiles; closed form theta = -2 s0 tan(s0 (v-a)) verified symbolically; the two escapes shown as such (sigma = 0 identically gives theta = 0 -- the generic condition is load-bearing; Casimir R_kk < 0 with sigma = 0 gives theta(B) = +1.13 > 0, defocusing as eq. (11)). (3b) z3: eqs (5)-(8) as a real-arithmetic implication -- K_{a;b} Z^a Z^b >= 0 from Z^3_{;b} Z^b <= 0 and K^3 > 0 is unsat to refute; theta >= 0 at B follows; jointly unsat with eq. (4); vacuity guard passes. (4) composite.py's vacuum ray with Weyl shear only: theta(B) = -1.4e-3 < 0, so Olum's Condition 1 cannot hold on it. NOT machine-checked, accepted as READ: the causal-structure steps (P is a null geodesic normal to both surfaces; no point of P conjugate to Sigma_A; invertibility of the congruence map A -> B) -- standard Hawking-Ellis propositions restated verbatim by Lobo-Crawford sec. 4.

later_literature.ref: Visser, Bassett, Liberati, 'Superluminal censorship', gr-qc/9810026 (Nucl. Phys. B Proc. Suppl. 88, 267, 2000)
later_literature.what: Perturbative around Minkowski in Hilbert-Lorentz gauge: NEC => light cones contract, Shapiro delay never an advance. Explicitly 'complementary to [Olum]' and 'we do not yet have a fully convincing argument that applies in a non-perturbative setting' (sec. 4). This, not Olum's theorem, is the reference-geometry 'lead' result the tree's spec.py/foliation D4 need -- and it is weak-field only.

later_literature.ref: Gao & Wald, 'Theorems on gravitational time delay and related issues', gr-qc/0007021 (CQG 17, 4999, 2000)
later_literature.what: NEC + null generic condition, no reference geometry. Theorem 1: fastest null geodesics between points outside a compact K' avoid K -- 'it is difficult to make a strong argument for this interpretation, since the theorem gives little control over the size of K'' (p.10). Theorem 2: time delay in asymptotically AdS. Also records (p.3) that VBL's conclusion is gauge-dependent and reversible in any compact region by a pure-gauge perturbation, and (p.4) that under the DEC a spacetime flat outside a world-tube (Olum's p.3 setting) is impossible by the positive mass theorem. Footnote 1: Galloway's null-line version strengthens Theorem 1.

later_literature.ref: Lobo & Crawford, 'Weak energy condition violation and superluminal travel', gr-qc/0204038 (2002)
later_literature.what: Restates Condition 1 and the proof step by step (sec. 4), same hypotheses and conclusion; notes the CTC extension is open. Eq. (33) misprints Olum's eq. (10) by a factor pi (sympy, this pass). Their Condition (ii) is written 'if and only if' where Olum writes 'only if' -- a restatement drift in the direction of a stronger premise.

later_literature.ref: Santiago, Schuster & Visser, 'Generic warp drives violate the null energy condition', arXiv:2105.03079 (PRD 105, 064038, 2022)
later_literature.what: Every generic Natario warp drive (Alcubierre, zero-expansion, Lentz/Fell-Heisenberg zero-vorticity, Bobrick-Martire) violates the NEC 'using only the fact that warp drive contributions are sufficiently localized' (sec. 7.4); Eulerian positivity alone never establishes the WEC (sec. 5). Independent of Olum's Condition 1; same direction.

later_literature.ref: Lentz, 'Hyper-fast positive energy warp drives', arXiv:2201.00652 (MG16 proceedings, 2021)
later_literature.what: Claims a WEC-satisfying superluminal soliton and argues (sec. 4) that Olum's and Lobo-Crawford's proofs are 'very local', 'analogous to collapsing the interior of a warp drive soliton to a point', and that his soliton 'exists outside their scope'; disputes SSV's divergence-theorem step on smoothness grounds. No counterexample to Condition 1 + generic + NEC is exhibited; the claim is that the hypotheses are not met.

later_literature.ref: Celmaster & Rubin, 'Violations of the weak energy condition for Lentz warp drives', arXiv:2511.18251 (2025)
later_literature.what: Direct computation: Lentz's geometry has regions of negative Eulerian energy density (Fig. 4), his potential does not solve his own differential equation (sign error), and two corrected variants also violate the WEC; 'no Natario warp-drive has been demonstrated to comply with the WEC' (sec. 7). Removes the only published candidate counterexample in the literature read.

later_literature.what: Positive-mass argument from geodesic advancement; Olum records it 'also discusses the connection between WEC violation and geodesic advancement'.

lacked_data: The theorem takes no measured input: its premises are Einstein's equation, an energy condition on one null geodesic, the generic condition, and a causal-structure definition; the re-derivation here reproduces it from those alone. So M's hypothesis -- that the authors lacked data that would change the conclusion -- has no purchase on this result, and the evidence is the script: nothing in it can be moved by a datum. What Olum did lack in 1998 and what came later, each checked: (i) the 2021 positive-energy warp-drive claims (Lentz, Bobrick-Martire, Fell-Heisenberg) were the only later work that purported to reach past the theorem, and Santiago-Schuster-Visser 2021 (generic NEC violation) and Celmaster-Rubin 2025 (Lentz's drive has negative Eulerian density; derivation errors) removed them -- evidence FOR the conclusion, not against; (ii) Gao-Wald 2000 showed VBL's reference-geometry 'lead' result is gauge-dependent -- this narrows the tree's 'lead' claim, not Olum's theorem; (iii) quantum inequalities (Ford-Roman, later Fewster et al.) tightened the loophole Olum himself names on p.6 ('the weak energy condition is not obeyed by systems of quantum fields') -- they constrain the escape, they do not touch the theorem. The one place the conclusion could move is not data but theory: replace Einstein's equation and H3 becomes the null convergence condition R_ab K^a K^b >= 0 directly, and the theorem reads 'superluminal travel requires NCC violation on P' -- still a no-go, differently named.
grade_evidence: The published theorem STANDS at source: read in full, re-derived with 0 failures (Raychaudhuri step exact and numeric, eqs (5)-(8) machine-checked in z3 with a vacuity guard), no datum enters it, and every later paper read either restates it (Lobo-Crawford), extends it in the same direction (VBL, Gao-Wald, SSV), or attacked its scope and was itself refuted (Lentz -> Celmaster-Rubin). The tree's USE is narrower than it states at four owners: (a) the generic condition (H2) is dropped by ledger D5, spec.py:106-107/198, composite.py:116-117, foliation.py:74-77/235-240 and specthm SR3 -- the rederivation shows it is load-bearing (shear = 0 gives theta(B) = 0, no contradiction); (b) spec.py:106-107, specthm.py:1367-1371 and foliation.py:235-240 use the theorem for 'a lead relative to a reference geometry', which is not Condition 1 (Olum p.4 says his condition may not be sufficient for that), so what actually backs the 'lead' sentence is Olum's p.3 special case (flat outside a bounded region; WEC violated somewhere in the region, not on the path) or the perturbative, gauge-dependent VBL result -- a smaller class with a weaker conclusion than 'pointwise on the path travelled'; (c) composite.py:116-117 cites the theorem for negative energy the ray never crosses, which the theorem does not say (rederivation (4)). driven.py:109-114 and ledger D5's 'no staticity, no symmetry, no sphericity, pointwise on the path' are faithful, and DOCKET_PREMISE_WAS_TRUE = False (driven.py:484) is correctly annotated. Two misprints recorded, neither a refutation: Olum's '(1+sqrt5)/2 ~ 0.618' (should be (sqrt5-1)/2) and Lobo-Crawford's factor-pi in eq. (33). Nothing in the tree is repaired by this audit.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the four owners restate H1 as Condition 1 (locally earliest path, 2-surface construction) plus the generic condition, and the 'lead' sentences (spec.py:106-107, :198; specthm SR3; foliation D4) cite the result that actually covers a reference-geometry advance -- Olum p.3 (H5, WEC violated somewhere in the bounded modified region) or VBL (weak field, Hilbert-Lorentz gauge) -- with that result's own hypotheses; composite.py:116-117 drops the Olum citation or names Gao-Wald's Jacobi-matrix optics as what it uses. To WRONG: an explicit spacetime with a path satisfying Condition 1 and the generic condition on which R_ab K^a K^b >= 0 everywhere -- none exists in the literature read; Lentz's candidate did not survive Celmaster-Rubin. To DATA-DEPENDENT: impossible as the theorem stands, since no measured quantity enters it. To OPEN: nothing -- the source was read at alphaXiv in full.
